task: Reveal-Position Bias Analysis for EBR (Condition C)
exclusion_reason: 1 run had paid proposal outside the batch of 3 (arrival rank 5)

interpretation.finding: EBR successfully eliminates arrival-order bias (arrival-rank distribution ~uniform, chi2 p=0.49 from prior analysis). However, it introduces a strong list-position primacy bias: the 1st proposal in the shuffled batch is selected 72.7% of the time, virtually identical to HardGate's 73.3% arrival-order bias rate. The bias has not been eliminated — it has shifted from temporal ordering to presentation ordering.
interpretation.implication: Sequential visibility is causal for arrival-order bias, confirming the EBR mechanism works as intended. However, the underlying LLM primacy bias (preference for the first item in any list) is a deeper confound that persists regardless of whether proposals arrive sequentially or are presented simultaneously.
interpretation.recommendation: To fully debias, recommend: (1) forced pairwise comparison step, (2) rotating presentation order across multiple LLM calls and aggregating, or (3) structured evaluation prompt that scores each proposal independently before comparing.

comparison_with_hardgate.note: EBR successfully randomizes which arrival-rank ends up first, but the LLM still picks whatever is listed first ~73% of the time
